text:
nina (AE): Starting a concise presales thread for Prospect: Meridian Labs. They want to replace Veridian endpoints with Redwood while keeping client SDK unchanged. Main asks: prompt parity, billing comparability, rate-limit behavior, and an enterprise security packet.

raj (SE): Good checklist. For the shim POC we'll need: 1) their canonical SDK request bodies (Go/Python/JS samples), 2) 20 representative prompts (short, long, multi-turn), 3) a small ground-truth set of expected responses or acceptance criteria for each prompt. Also traffic shape (burst qps, sustained qps, percent long seqs).

claire (Solutions Eng): I'll run response-delta checks. Plan: deterministic equality for templated prompts, KL/divergence on token distributions for open prompts, and a "soft-match" list of anchors to flag unacceptable hallucinations. Deliverable: one-page parity summary + 5 example failure cases. ETA 36 hours after we get samples.

tom (Infra): For the hosted POC we can expose a compatibility route that accepts Veridian payloads and proxies to Redwood models. We need their test IPs to lock down the route and a note if they need client certs. If Meridian wants an on-prem/VPC option later, that requires a short infra scoping call.

ana (Security): (typo: ana) Please send over the vendor questionnaire PDF; I'll pre-fill everything we control. Quick callouts: SOC2 status, encryption-at-rest (KMS), TLS mutual auth supported on Private, audit logs retention, and data purging options. Also list of subcomponents with their PCI/ISO attestations if requested.

nina (AE): They also asked about subtle output formatting differences that broke downstream parsers in a prior vendor swap. Can we provide a safe fallback mode that outputs strict JSON vs free text?

claire (Solutions Eng): Yes — we'll enable structured-output mode and a JSON schema enforcement layer in the shim. Example: set header X-Redwood-Mode: strict-json and the response will include "parsed_output" field and an "errors" array if validation fails. We'll include a short example in the POC docs.

raj (SE): Also recommend running a small randomized prompt mutation test to surface brittle regex-based parsers. I can add a tiny harness that mutates whitespace/punctuation and checks parser acceptance rates.

billing-bot: Note: POC keys are rate-limited to 60 rps and 200k tokens/day by default. Contact billing for quota bump.

nina (AE): Meridian is sensitive about cost predictability. They asked if we do committed Dedicated credits proration when they upgrade mid-contract. Tom/billing: what's the quick answer?

billing-bot: Short answer: proration is handled case-by-case; typical pattern: apply unused Hosted spend toward Dedicated commitment on a pro-rata basis for the remainder of the billing period. We'll open a formal quote after usage review.

tom (Infra): One more infra note: if they have many long-context requests (>8k tokens) we'll advise a larger model slice or a quantized variant to keep p95 latency under their SLA. We'll include a small cost/latency table in the POC handoff.

claire (Solutions Eng): For metrics in the report: token-delta histogram, top-10 ngram diffs, percent-anchor-match, and p95 latency under their target qps. We'll also capture a few human-eval labels for sensitive prompts if they want.

ana (Security): I'll attach a one-page summary: SSO options (SAML/OIDC), KMS integrations, retention and deletion controls, and our recommended secure deployment pattern. Also ask Meridian to mark any regulatory constraints (PCI, HIPAA, GDPR).

nina (AE): Timeline: customer wants a short demo + parity report in 5 business days. Is that realistic?

raj (SE): If assets arrive by EOD tomorrow (prompts + SDK samples + test CIDR) we can deliver a smoke compatibility shim + parity report within 4 business days. Runner-up tasks: provisioning POC key, allowlist, and small docs for their QA team.

nina (AE): I'll request assets right away and include the test CIDR. Also looping Legal to check their standard vendor addendum.

billing-bot: Action created: quote-request-1744444444. Assigned to billing ops.

tom (Infra): I'll provision a POC key and a dedicated staging route once I have the CIDR. Quick curl example for their QA:```bash
curl -X POST https://poc.redwood.internal/compat/veridian/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"client_id":"abc123","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize quarterly progress"}],"max_tokens":150}'
```Response includes fields mapped to Veridian keys: status, output_text, usage_tokens.

claire (Solutions Eng): I'll add a small sample harness and the strict-json header example to the repo we hand to Meridian.

nina (AE): Thanks team. I'll ping back once Meridian shares artifacts. Keeping this thread as the canonical presales coordination channel. :white_check_mark:
